dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine. How can I help you this afternoon?
Good afternoon. Yes, my name is Leila Goldberg. I am calling about the water at the curb in front of my house. It is on Eustis Avenue.
Okay, Mrs. Goldberg. Can you give me the house number on Eustis?
Two hundred eighty-nine. Two eight nine Eustis Avenue. Up on the Hill.
Two eighty-nine Eustis Avenue. And what's happening with the water?

Well, it is not raining. There is no storm, nothing. But the snow melts in the afternoon, the sun comes, and the water runs down and sits at the curb. It makes a big puddle. Then at night it freezes, and in the morning it is ice. Black ice, you cannot see it. Somebody is going to slip. [pause] Ai, meu Deus.
That's a real hazard. So it's ponding right at the curb, and it's not draining off during the day?

No, it does not go anywhere. The drain, I think it is stopped. Every day the same. I am the landlord there, I have tenants, and they come and go with the groceries, with the little bags. And next door there is an older gentleman, he is older than me almost, and he cannot get out. He is afraid to walk down to the street with this ice.
I understand. So your neighbor next door is having trouble getting out of the house because of the ice by the curb.
Yes, exactly. He stays inside. His daughter does not live here. So he waits.
Okay. Let me make sure I have it right. Two eighty-nine Eustis Avenue, meltwater collecting at the curb during the day, freezing overnight, and the nearby storm drain may be blocked. Is that right?
Yes, that is right. You say it better than me. My English, it is slow, I am sorry.
No, you're doing fine. Take your time. How long has this been going on?
Over a week now. Maybe ten days. And I want to know, when did they last come by? Somebody from the city, to look at this drain, to clean it. Because I do not see anybody. Nobody comes.
That's a fair question. I don't have the cleaning record in front of me for that block. Let me pull up the address and see what's logged. Can you hold for a minute?

Yes, yes. I wait. [pause] Excuse me, I have the television on, I am going to put it down. The batteries in the remote control died in the middle of my program. Just like that. So I am sitting here with no volume, no nothing.
Oh, that's always at the best part. Let me look. One moment.
Of course. Take your time.

Okay, Mrs. Goldberg, I'm back. I'm not seeing a recent work order for that stretch of Eustis. There's nothing logged for the drain there in the last while that I can see. So I can't tell you a date for the last visit.
Nothing? Nothing at all? So nobody has come. This is what I think. I pay my taxes, I am here a long time, and nobody comes to look.

I hear you. What I can do is open a new request right now, mark it as an ice hazard because of the freezing, and send it to the crew that handles drains. I can't promise you the hour they'll arrive, but I'll flag it so it doesn't sit.
Please, yes. Please say it is ice, and an old man next door. That is important. Somebody will fall and break a hip. At our age, that is the end.
I'll put that in the notes: elderly neighbor, difficulty leaving the house, black ice forming overnight. Is there a phone number where they can reach you if they have questions?
Yes. Four zero one, five five five, zero one eight four.
Four-oh-one, five-five-five, zero-one-eight-four. Got it. And is the puddle right in front of two eighty-nine, or is it closer to the corner?
In front of my house, a little toward the neighbor's side. Where the curb goes down a little. It is a low place.
In front, toward the neighbor's side at the low spot in the curb. Okay. That's all in the request.
Thank you. And if I put some salt, is that okay? I have a little salt for the steps.
That's fine to do on your own walkway and steps. It won't fix the drain, but it'll help people walking. Just keep it on your property side as best you can.
Yes, I will do that today. And I will wait for the crew. You will call me if there is a problem?
If the crew needs anything, they'll use that number. And if it's still frozen and nobody's been out in a couple of days, call us back and mention this request.
Thank you, Lorraine. You are very patient with me. Good afternoon.
You're welcome, Mrs. Goldberg. Take care, and watch your step out there.
